tips.title: While an elderly parent is still lucid, put the care decisions in writing — India has no adult guardianship statute, so the tools are a will, a bank mandate and, for mental illness, an advance directive
tips.cost: A notary charges a small fee to attest a document, and registering a deed at the sub-registrar costs more. The real cost is time: the conversation takes an evening, and getting the paperwork right takes a few visits.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no law that lets an adult appoint a general guardian who takes over their affairs if they later lose capacity. The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 deals with minors. For an adult with one of the disabilities covered by the National Trust Act, 1999, a limited guardian can be appointed. For mental illness, the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 lets a person make an advance directive and nominate a representative. In practice families use a will for property, a joint holder or a mandate for bank accounts, and a written family agreement for day-to-day care. A power of attorney is useful while the person still has capacity, but it is not guardianship and a bank or hospital can refuse it once capacity is in doubt.
tips.benefit: Write down four things while the parent can still sign: a will under the Indian Succession Act, 1925 naming who inherits and who is the executor; a list of every bank account, with a joint holder or a mandate so that bills can still be paid; the names and numbers of the treating doctors and the hospital the family prefers; and a note of who decides what, day to day. Keep the originals where two family members can find them, and give copies to the doctor and the bank. If the parent later develops a mental illness, an advance directive and a nominated representative under the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 give the doctors a named person to speak to.
tips.sources: Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Mental Healthcare Act, 2017. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Trust for the Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. <https://socialjustice.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A power of attorney is not a guardianship order, and a dispute over it goes to court. An unregistered will is valid but must be proved after death, so the witnesses must still be findable. A family agreement has no statutory force of its own; it works because everyone signed it, and it is the document a court reads first if the family falls out. Do not let one sibling hold every original.

tips.title: Make a will — a later will revokes an earlier one, and a notarised will has no special priority in Indian law
tips.cost: A typed will costs nothing but the paper. A lawyer may charge a fee to draft one, notarising costs a small fee, and registration at the sub-registrar is optional and costs more. The expensive mistake is not the fee, it is a will that is unsigned or unwitnessed.
tips.inPlainWords: Under the Indian Succession Act, 1925 a will must be in writing, signed by the testator, and attested by two or more witnesses who each saw the testator sign. There is no list of will types in Indian law and no rule that a will must be handwritten. A notarised or registered will has no legal priority over an unregistered one; registration only makes the document easier to prove. If more than one will exists, the last valid one governs, because a later will revokes an earlier one.
tips.benefit: Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 sets the form: writing, the testator's signature, and attestation by two or more witnesses who are present at the same time. Registration at the sub-registrar under the Registration Act, 1908 is optional. Name an executor — the person who will apply for probate where probate is needed — and be specific about every asset: the flat's address, the bank and branch, the account, the jewellery. A will can be changed at any time by a new will or a codicil, and the newest one wins.
tips.sources: Indian Succession Act, 1925, section 63. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Registration Act, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Law and Justice. <https://lawmin.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Two witnesses must see you sign, and each must sign in your presence; a will signed alone and witnessed on a later day is easier to challenge. Keep the original where a family member can find it, and tell the executor that it exists. A bank or insurance nomination decides who collects the money, but the nominee holds it for the people who inherit under the will, so keep the nomination and the will consistent.

tips.title: Keep the elderly person’s money in a separate account and set a rule requiring two people to approve any large withdrawals
tips.cost: This costs nothing. You only need to discuss it once with family members and agree on a spending limit. The real challenge is how to bring it up without making the senior feel you’re trying to restrict them.
tips.inPlainWords: Scammers targeting seniors for health products, collectibles, or financial schemes all follow the same pattern: they spend months building rapport, then strike all at once. By establishing a rule that any withdrawal above a certain amount must be approved by another person, you effectively delay the spending decision until the initial impulse fades.
tips.benefit: Most scams aimed at older adults rely on building trust over weeks or months before making a large financial demand. Setting a rule that requires a second person’s approval for any sizable expenditure helps delay that decision, reducing the chance of impulsive, costly mistakes.
tips.sources: Author’s experience, no direct literature; see Sections 8 and 13 for general anti-fraud rules; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. <https://socialjustice.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Frame this not as “protecting them from fraud” but as “keeping household finances organized.” That approach is far easier for seniors to accept. Also, avoid moving all of their money into a child’s account — doing so can lead to entirely different kinds of disputes.

tips.title: A ready-made phrase for seniors to deflect unwanted offers
tips.cost: No cost at all. It only takes a few minutes to discuss this with the senior once.
tips.inPlainWords: Sales pitches and scams rely on creating immediate pressure, making it hard for people to say no on the spot. By agreeing beforehand on the phrase “I need to go home and discuss this with my family,” the senior has an easy way out whenever needed. This works far better than trying to reason with them later.
tips.benefit: Both sales tactics and scams depend on on‑the‑spot pressure. Having a pre‑arranged line such as “I need to go home and discuss this with my family” gives seniors a graceful exit, making it far more effective than any post‑event explanation.
tips.sources: author’s experience, no direct literature; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. <https://socialjustice.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Use this together with tip #3 (keeping the senior’s money in a separate account). You can also carry out home modifications to prevent falls, as described in Section 1. This phrase isn’t meant to protect the senior from themselves; it simply provides a way to decline politely without feeling awkward. When surrounded by salespeople, the hardest part isn’t judging whether they’re trustworthy — it’s finding the courage to say no in front of everyone. Agreeing on this line beforehand removes that burden entirely.

tips.title: Avoid 'investment-based' senior-care schemes that demand a large upfront payment
tips.cost: A legitimate facility charges a monthly fee and a refundable deposit; a 'guaranteed return' scheme is a red flag.
tips.inPlainWords: A scheme that asks an older person to pay a large deposit for lifetime care, a membership card or a 'guaranteed' return is a credit and fraud risk. India has no regulator for a prepaid senior-care deposit. The safe routes are a registered senior-living facility with a written contract, the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme, and the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007. Do not sign over property for a promise of care.
tips.benefit: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 allows a senior citizen to claim maintenance from a child or a relative and provides for a tribunal. The Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme is a government small-saving product. A senior-living facility should be a registered entity with a written agreement, a clear refund clause and a complaint route. The RBI and SEBI have warned against unauthorised deposit and investment schemes.
tips.sources: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. <https://socialjustice.gov.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, unauthorised schemes. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Securities and Exchange Board of India. <https://www.sebi.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A 'lifetime care' promise is only as good as the company. A transfer of property for care should be a registered deed with a life interest. Take a lawyer and a family member to the signing.

tips.title: Apart from a reverse mortgage loan from a bank or housing finance company, avoid every 'housing-for-pension' scheme — never mortgage your home to buy a financial product
tips.cost: A reverse mortgage carries valuation, legal and processing fees charged by the lender, and the loan is repaid with interest out of the sale of the house. Refusing a salesman costs nothing.
tips.inPlainWords: A reverse mortgage is a loan against a house, offered by some banks and housing finance companies: the owner keeps living in the home, and the lender recovers the loan and interest from the sale of the house later. India runs no state pilot for this and sells no 'reverse mortgage insurance' product, so anyone presenting one is selling something else. The test is simple: the money must come from a regulated lender under a written loan agreement, not from a scheme that asks you to transfer the property or to invest in a fund in return for a monthly payment.
tips.benefit: Banks and housing finance companies may offer reverse mortgage loans under the Reserve Bank of India's framework, and a pension-linked version has been permitted in which the amount drawn is used to buy an annuity, so the borrower receives a monthly income. Both are contracts with a regulated entity, and both reduce what is left for the heirs. Any other 'housing for pension' offer — hand over the flat and we pay you monthly — is an unregulated private arrangement with no statutory protection and no route to recover the property.
tips.sources: Reserve Bank of India. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>; Ministry of Finance. <https://finmin.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: The yield warnings are rules of thumb, not statutory thresholds: a scheme promising a guaranteed 6, 8 or 10 per cent return on a property-backed product is a warning sign, not a regulated rate. Read whether the house has to be transferred, who pays maintenance and property tax, and what happens if the owner has to move into a care home. Show the agreement to a family member and a lawyer before signing, and never sign a blank or undated document. For an ordinary monthly pension instead, see item 5.

tips.title: For a bedridden or severely disabled elder at home, ask the scheme and the district for home-based care
tips.cost: PM-JAY is free for eligible households. A private home-nursing service is paid.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no single 'home care' benefit, but there are routes: PM-JAY for eligible households, ESIC for insured workers, the state health department's palliative-care and home-care programmes, and the district disability office for an assessment and a certificate. Ayushman Arogya Mandir and ASHA workers can visit. Ask the district health officer what home-based palliative care exists.
tips.benefit: PM-JAY covers hospitalisation and some packages; the state health department may run home-based palliative care through medical colleges and NGOs. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 provides for a disability certificate, an assessment and some concessions. ESIC provides medical benefit to insured persons and dependants. The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly provides geriatric services at some district hospitals.
tips.sources: National Health Authority, PM-JAY. <https://nha.gov.in/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. <https://depwd.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, elderly care. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>; Employees' State Insurance Corporation. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A disability certificate is issued after an assessment by a medical board; it is not automatic. A home-care NGO should be verified. Keep the treatment records.

tips.title: For families with someone bedridden at home, pressure ulcers are a top concern: use an electric alternating-pressure air mattress, turn the patient regularly, and check bony areas daily
tips.cost: An electric alternating-pressure air mattress is not a small purchase: an entry-level home unit costs several thousand rupees and a hospital-grade one costs more, so check the price and the service terms before ordering. Turning a patient takes a couple of minutes. The real cost is the schedule — every two to three hours, day and night, which no single carer can sustain alone.
tips.inPlainWords: Pressure ulcers are far more than just superficial skin injuries. Among older adults undergoing hip-fracture surgery, those already having pressure ulcers at admission face a roughly 20% higher chance of dying within 30 days. Three evidence‑based actions help: using an electric air mattress cuts new ulcer formation by about 60% compared with ordinary hospital mattresses; consistently turning the patient reduces risk by roughly 70% versus standard care; and keeping the person from lying prone for long periods also helps. Check the sacrum, heels, hips, and shoulders each day; if any area shows persistent redness that doesn’t fade when pressed, contact a nurse or doctor right away.
tips.benefit: Data come from 19,520 hip‑fracture patients in the U.S. NSQIP registry (2016‑2019). Those with pre‑existing pressure ulcers showed a higher 30‑day mortality rate; after adjusting for other factors, this link remained significant (OR 1.2, a 21% increase in risk, P = 0.004). They also faced higher rates of deep‑vein thrombosis (OR 1.59), pneumonia (OR 1.39), unplanned readmissions (OR 1.43), and an average hospital stay 0.4 days longer. In a follow‑up of 324 elderly inpatients (mean age 86) over 18 months, pressure ulcers independently predicted long‑term death (HR 1.500, 95% CI 1.059‑2.126, P = 0.020). A network meta‑analysis of 65 randomized trials compared electric alternating‑pressure air mattresses with standard hospital mattresses; the former lowered ulcer incidence (RR 0.42, 95% CI 0.29‑0.63, moderate certainty). Similar benefits were seen with hybrid systems (RR 0.22, 95% CI 0.07‑0.66). A 2026 Cochrane review of 11 trials involving 4,462 patients found little difference between turning schedules of 2 hours versus 4 hours (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.79‑1.39, very low certainty). However, using wearable sensors to enforce 2‑hour turning intervals in an ICU setting cut ulcer rates compared with usual care (RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.10‑0.75, moderate certainty). Finally, patients kept in a prone position developed ulcers far more often than those lying supine (RR 4.55, 95% CI 2.31‑8.98).
tips.sources: Porter SB, Pla R, Chow JH, et al. (2022). Preoperative Pressure Ulcers, Mortality, and Complications in Older Hip Fracture Surgery Patients. JAAOS Global Research & Reviews, 6(11). <https://doi.org/10.5435/JAAOSGlobal-D-22-00117>; Ottaviani S, Rondanina E, Longo E, et al. (2026). Impact of pressure ulcers and frailty on long-term mortality: a prospective cohort study of hospitalized older adults. European Geriatric Medicine, 17(2), 665-672. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s41999-025-01331-8>; Shi C, Dumville JC, Cullum N (2018). Support surfaces for pressure ulcer prevention: A network meta-analysis. PLoS ONE, 13(2), e0192707. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0192707>; Latimer SL, Chaboyer WP, Probst S, et al. (2026). Repositioning for pressure injury prevention in adults. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 6, CD009958. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD009958.pub4>; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. <https://socialjustice.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: This grade reflects three main points. First, the mortality studies showed only that patients with ulcers fared worse; they did not prove that preventing ulcers directly lowers death rates. Second, the evidence on optimal turning intervals from randomized trials is quite weak. Third, the data on air mattresses are relatively stronger, yet they compared hospital‑grade mattresses to ordinary home mattresses, so extrapolation to home use is somewhat uncertain. Daily inspection of bony areas is standard nursing practice and lacks dedicated research support. The mortality benefit is evaluated separately from cost calculations for other items in this section. Home-based care — a hired attendant, home nursing, or a day-care centre — is described in item 7. India has no long-term care insurance scheme for this, so the family pays, and the cost of an attendant is the largest recurring item. Sudden leg swelling should be treated as a possible deep‑vein thrombosis, as covered in section 13, item 11. Situations involving prolonged bed rest after falls or severe injury are discussed in section 1, item 34.

tips.title: If cataract is affecting walking safely, get an eye assessment; surgery is free in a government hospital
tips.cost: Free at a government hospital under the programme; about ₹15,000–₹40,000 per eye in a private hospital, depending on the lens.
tips.inPlainWords: A cataract that makes walking or reading unsafe should be assessed by an ophthalmologist. The National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment provides free cataract surgery at government hospitals and through camp-based programmes in many districts. If both eyes are affected, the surgeon usually operates on one eye first. Do not wait until the cataract is 'ripe'.
tips.benefit: The National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment funds cataract surgery and screening at district hospitals and vision centres. A government hospital provides a free intraocular lens; a private hospital charges. The surgery is usually day-care, and the first eye is operated before the second. An untreated cataract can lead to falls and a loss of independence.
tips.sources: National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment. <https://npcbvi.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>; All India Institute of Medical Sciences, ophthalmology. <https://www.aiims.edu/>
tips.caveats: The waiting period varies by district. A 'free' camp should be a government or a registered NGO camp. Bring the Aadhaar or another ID for the hospital record.

tips.title: When elderly family members walk dogs: Hold the leash in the palm rather than wrapping it around hands or wrists, keep the lead short, and train the dog not to surge forward
tips.cost: Gripping the leash properly and shortening lead length costs nothing—simply walk with your elder once to demonstrate proper technique. Training a dog not to surge takes time, either trained personally or through a professional trainer (incurring variable local fees). The main difficulty is changing ingrained habits if seniors are accustomed to retractable leashes or tightly wrapping webbing around their wrists.
tips.inPlainWords: In the United States, annual fractures among adults aged 65 and older associated with walking leashed dogs surged from roughly 1,700 to 4,400 cases, with women accounting for nearly 80%. The hip was the single most common fracture site, and nearly 30% of patients required hospitalization. Among patients sustaining hand injuries from dog leashes, approximately three-quarters occurred when a sudden jerk tightened a leash wrapped around the hand or fingers. Keep the leash gripped in the palm, maintain a short lead, and train dogs not to pull aggressively.
tips.benefit: US national emergency department surveillance data estimate that annual fractures among individuals aged 65 and older walking leashed dogs rose from 1,671 in 2004 to 4,396 in 2017—a statistically significant increase. Among fracture victims, 78.6% were women and 28.7% required inpatient hospital admission. By anatomical site, hip fractures were the most frequent single injury (17.3%), while upper extremity fractures comprised 52.1% across broad categories. Another nationwide emergency database covering 2001–2018 estimated 356,746 dog-leash-related injuries: 193,483 involved being pulled down or strained by a dog, and 136,767 involved tripping or entanglement. Population injury rates climbed from 25.4 to 105.5 per million individuals. In a 5-year study at an outpatient hand surgery clinic reviewing 443 leash-related hand injuries, 75.9% (337 patients) occurred when a leash wrapped around the hand or fingers was abruptly yanked by the dog, and 21.6% (96 patients) required surgical intervention. CDC surveillance (2001–2006) showed approximately 86,629 fall-related injuries annually involving pet cats and dogs, with 88.0% attributable to dogs; 26% occurred while walking dogs, and 21.2% were caused by dogs pushing or pulling their handlers.
tips.sources: Pirruccio K, Yoon YM, Ahn J (2019). Fractures in Elderly Americans Associated With Walking Leashed Dogs. JAMA Surgery, 154(5), 458-459. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamasurg.2019.0061>; Forrester MB (2020). Dog leash-related injuries treated at emergency departments. American Journal of Emergency Medicine, 38(9), 1782-1786. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajem.2020.05.082>; Plusch K, Givner D, Wiafe B, Lutsky K, Beredjiklian P (2026). Hand and Wrist Dog-Leash Injuries in the Outpatient Setting: A Review of 443 Cases. Hand, 21(4), 582-586. <https://doi.org/10.1177/15589447241299128>; CDC (2009). Nonfatal fall-related injuries associated with dogs and cats — United States, 2001-2006. MMWR, 58(11), 277-281. <https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/mm5811a1.htm>; Rosa R, Buckley RE (2024). Leash-related injuries associated with dog walking: an understudied risk for dog owners? Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association, 262(7), 973-978. <https://doi.org/10.2460/javma.23.11.0608>
tips.caveats: Gripping the leash firmly in the palm without wrapping it around fingers or wrists is explicitly recommended by hand surgeons: it protects fingers and wrists against spiral fractures and degloving injuries, though it does not completely prevent falls caused by aggressive surges. Keeping the lead short prevents the dog from building kinetic momentum and reduces trip hazards. Extended retractable leashes function as hazardous long lines; however, no controlled trials have isolated fall incidence between retractable versus standard fixed leashes (noted in a 2024 JAVMA review). Behavioral loose-leash training is recommended by both the CDC and orthopedic trauma researchers. For seniors considering adopting a new pet, researchers recommend smaller, lower-mass breeds. Benefit magnitude is rated small as exact reduction percentages for these combined interventions have not been evaluated in randomized trials. For bone fracture resilience, see Chapter 1, Rule 39 (bone mineral density screening) and Rule 40 (osteoporosis medication). For elder balance training, see Chapter 1, Rule 13. For counting dog walking toward daily physical activity goals, see Chapter 2, Rule 44. Beneficiaries are elderly parents and grandparents.

tips.title: Before placing an elderly relative in a care home, check its registration and sign a written contract — India has no national deposit cap, so the contract is the only protection
tips.cost: No fee to ask. The cost is a few visits: the district health office, the home itself, and a lawyer if the contract is long. A deposit is the real money at risk, so never pay it in cash.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no national filing system, deposit cap or escrow rule for elder-care homes. What exists is state-level: nursing homes and clinical establishments register under state nursing-home rules or under the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010 in the states that have adopted it, and a home for a person with a disability may fall under the National Trust Act, 1999. The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 gives an elderly person a route against neglect and for maintenance. Ask for the registration certificate, inspect the kitchen and the toilet, talk to two residents' families, and get every promise into the written agreement.
tips.benefit: A registered clinical establishment is inspected against minimum standards, and the state health authority can act on a complaint. The agreement should state the monthly fee, what is included and excluded, the notice period, the refund rule for the deposit, who is called in a medical emergency, and what happens if the resident's needs increase. Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 a senior citizen who is unable to maintain himself can apply to the maintenance tribunal, and the state has a welfare responsibility for senior citizens' homes. Keep receipts for every payment.
tips.sources: Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. <https://socialjustice.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: No central rule caps the deposit, so a large 'lifetime' deposit is the main risk: pay by bank transfer, get a receipt, and put the refund formula in the contract. Ask what the home does when a resident becomes bed-bound — many quietly ask the family to move the person. Check the fire exit and the doctor's visiting arrangement, and visit once without an appointment. If the home is unregistered, the district health authority and the state welfare department for senior citizens are the two places to complain.

tips.title: India has no statutory elder-care leave — use the leave your contract or company policy gives, and ask in writing the day a parent is admitted
tips.cost: Asking costs nothing. Unpaid leave costs the salary for those days. The expensive mistake is resigning first and asking afterwards.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no national or state statute that gives an only child paid leave to care for a hospitalised parent. What you can claim is the leave your own appointment letter, employment contract or company policy provides — earned or privilege leave, casual leave, sick leave, and any compassionate or family-care leave the employer's rules allow. Central government employees have earned leave under the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972; for a private employer the entitlement is contractual. Ask by email, attach the hospital's admission note, and keep a copy of the reply.
tips.benefit: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 and the state Shops and Establishments Acts set hours of work, weekly rest and leave entitlement for the workers they cover; none of them creates a right to elder-care leave, and the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 covers maternity only. So the enforceable right, when it exists, comes from the contract or the leave policy. Where the contract gives leave and the employer refuses it, the worker can complain to the state labour department, and a registered trade union can raise it as an industrial dispute. Read the appointment letter and the HR policy before you ask.
tips.sources: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (sections 25 and 32). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972. <https://dopt.gov.in/>; Ministry of Labour and Employment. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not resign to care for a parent before checking what leave you have and what notice your contract requires. A verbal promise of leave is hard to prove; ask by email and keep the reply. Leave without pay preserves the job but not the salary, and it may break continuity of service for gratuity. If the parent needs care for months rather than weeks, plan for hired help or a care home instead (item 11).

tips.title: If an elderly relative suffers progressive memory decline impairing daily functioning, visit a hospital memory clinic or neurology department to rule out reversible causes like depression, sensory deficits, or anticholinergic drugs
tips.cost: Low cost only if the family's own cover pays. India has no standard health insurance: a memory clinic visit, psychometric testing and blood and urine panels are usually paid out of pocket, and are covered only if the family's policy or employer scheme includes outpatient diagnostics. Budget half a day to a full day, and ask for the test list and the price before booking. The obstacle is often the elderly relative's own reluctance to be tested.
tips.inPlainWords: Progressive cognitive decline is not simply inevitable "old age." First rule out reversible conditions such as late-life depression, adverse drug side effects, and uncorrected hearing or vision loss. Truly reversible dementias are rare (under 1%), but early diagnosis serves another purpose: it lets the family put a will, a bank mandate and the day-to-day care decisions in writing while the person can still sign (items 1 and 2).
tips.benefit: UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE NG97) guidelines mandate that when dementia is suspected, clinicians must take comprehensive histories from both patient and family, perform physical examinations, order laboratory blood/urine tests to rule out reversible etiologies, and conduct validated cognitive testing. NICE guidelines specifically highlight four treatable or modifiable confounders: delirium, depression, sensory impairment (vision and hearing deficits), and high anticholinergic cognitive burden from medications. Once reversible factors are excluded, patients are referred to specialist memory clinics. A classic meta-analysis of 39 clinical studies encompassing 5,620 dementia patients found that 56.3% had Alzheimer's disease and 20.3% had vascular dementia; potentially reversible etiologies represented 9.0%, but actual clinical improvement occurred in only 0.6% (0.29% partial improvement, 0.31% full recovery). NICE recommends advance care planning while capacity remains, including naming the person who will decide on finances and on health care; in India the equivalent documents are a will and a power of attorney, and neither survives the loss of capacity automatically (items 1 and 2). The assessment itself usually happens in the neurology, psychiatry or geriatric medicine department of a government medical college or district hospital. India has no national dementia screening programme, so a family that notices a change has to ask for the assessment.
tips.sources: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2018). Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers (NICE NG97, Recommendations 1.1.12, 1.2.1, 1.2.2, 1.2.6). <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng97/chapter/Recommendations>; Clarfield AM (2003). The decreasing prevalence of reversible dementias: an updated meta-analysis. Archives of Internal Medicine, 163(18), 2219-2229. <https://doi.org/10.1001/archinte.163.18.2219>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. <https://socialjustice.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Graded Evidence Grade B based on clinical consensus guidelines and diagnostic cohort reviews. Benefit is categorized as Low because clinical reversibility is under 1% and no evidence indicates that early screening alters ultimate dementia mortality. Never discontinue medications unilaterally; bring medication boxes to consultation. For acute cognitive decline and gait ataxia following minor head trauma, see Chapter 13, Rule 10 (head CT for chronic subdural hematoma). Hearing aid fitting for cognitive maintenance is covered in Chapter 33, Rule 17. Crucially, while the person is still clear-minded, put a will in place (Chapter 17, Rule 2) and the family's care and money arrangements in writing (Chapter 17, Rule 1). Beneficiaries are elderly parents and grandparents.
